title: Quantity Rules for Sensors and Receivers on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
Billing manual section: how the quantity of a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program shipment is fixed.

## 1. Sensor refills (A4239)

1.1 A sensor refill ships the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply for every 30 days of supply, so its units are its supply days divided by 30, multiplied by that figure.

1.2 Its pieces are the supply days divided by 30, multiplied by the sensors the program's CGM model uses per 30 days (the sensors-per-30-days figure for the model).

1.3 A Dexcom G6 program also receives one transmitter for every Dexcom G6 transmitter life (in days) of supply, inside the same allowance; no other model receives a transmitter.

1.4 The sensors shipped follow the CGM model on the program, never a model the customer names that is not on the newest written order.

1.5 On the CGM Self-Pay Program the refill is charged at the model's cash price per 30-day sensor supply for the program's model, per 30 days of supply.

## 2. Receivers and readers (E2103)

2.1 A receiver or reader ships as one billing unit and only on tiers where a receiver or reader is covered.

2.2 A covered replacement receiver ships no earlier than the tier's minimum time between covered receivers, in calendar months, after the ship date of the previous receiver recorded on the program, counted in calendar months from that ship date with the same calendar day allowed (the last day of the month when that day does not exist).

2.3 Within the manufacturer warranty from the previous receiver's delivery, a failed receiver is the manufacturer's warranty replacement instead.

2.4 A customer who uses the smartphone app receives no receiver, and a receiver on a tier where receivers are not covered, or one requested before the replacement interval, is supplied only at the model's receiver cash price under the program's liability notice rule.

## 3. Replacements

A replacement never exceeds the units and pieces of the shipment it replaces.

## 4. Worked figures (hypothetical)

- Suppose a 90-day supply, an allowance of 1 unit per 30 days and a model using 3 sensors per 30 days: 90 days divided by 30 is 3 blocks, so the refill is 3 units and 9 sensors.
- Suppose a Dexcom G6 program with a 90-day transmitter life receives a 90-day refill: it also receives 1 transmitter, within the same 3 units.
- **Receiver interval.** Suppose an interval of 36 months and a previous receiver shipped on 31 May of a hypothetical year: the same calendar day 36 months later is 31 May three years on, and a covered replacement may ship on that day but not on 30 May. Suppose instead an interval of 9 months and a previous receiver shipped on 31 May: the following February has no 31st day, so the earliest day a covered replacement may ship is the last day of that February.
